texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23896643/ 1 The instant complaint has been filed U/s.200 of Cr.P.C., by the complainant alleging tha t, the accused persons have committed the offence punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"). 2. The complainant's case in nutshell is as under: That on 30.11.2022 while CW-1/PW-1 being the Food Safety Officer, having visited the shop premises of accused No.1, he being the Proprietor of Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Rice Traders, No.3, Nagasettyhalli Main Road, Bengaluru was found to be selling the Basmati Rice, manufactured and supplied by accused No.2 being Proprietor and Managing Director of M/s. Work 3 located at Sonipal Nearala Road, Dharmakanta Village, Sonipat District, Hariyana. The aforesaid official suspecting the quality and label conditions of the Basmati Rice packets of 1 Kg, proceeded to collect four packets of Basmati Rice of 1 Kg each by preparing Form No.VA of the Act and by serving the copy of the aforesaid Form on the accused No.1 in the presence of one independent witness by drawing mahazar. Thereafter, the PW-1 forwarded the aforesaid four samples of Basmati Rice packets by wrapping them in the thick brown paper by affixing the slip containing signature of the accused No.1 and Designated Officer attached to BBMP North Division, Bengaluru to the analysis by Food Analyst by intimating the accused No.1 regarding his right for independent examination at NABL Laboratory, which was refused by accused No.1. The aforesaid one sample of Rice packet was handed over to the Food Analyst along with Form No.VI and Specimen Seal Form and remaining three samples were handed over to the Designated Officer attached to BBMP, North Division, Bengaluru. 3. The Food Analyst vide report dated 13.12.2022 declared the sample i.e., Basmati Rice of 1 Kg as "Not Confirming to the FSS Regulations, 2011 as Thiamethoxam Pesticide is beyond the limits" thereby held the subject food as "Unsafe". Hence, the instant complaint. 4. The accused persons appeared on service of summons through their counsel and were released on bail. The copy of the complaint and other documents came to be furnished to them in compliance of Section 207 of Cr.P.C. 5. The substance of the accusation was recorded by reading over and explaining its contents to the accused persons, they denied the same and claimed to be tried. 6. The complainant in order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts, got examined three witnesses as PW's-1 to 3 and got marked in all 12 documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-7, Ex.P-7(a) to Ex.P-11 and got closed its side of evidence. 7. The statement of accused persons as contemplated U/s.313 of Cr.P.C., was recorded. The accused persons denied the incriminating evidence in the testimonies of the PW's-1 to 3 on their behalf and have not chosen to adduce their defence evidence. Food Safety Officer vs Anil Kumar on 30 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23896643/ 2 8. The compliance U/s.437(A) of Cr.P.C., was dispensed by accepting the earlier personal bonds and cash securities furnished by the accused persons at the time of being enlarged on bail. The counsel for the accused No.2 submitted the authority in support of his arguments. Thereby, the accused persons have committed the offences punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the FSS Act, 2006. 13. The Food Safety Officer by name Sri. G. Govindharaju arrayed as CW-1 in support of the allegations set out in the complaint, got examined himself as PW-1.
texts.arguments: The learned Sr. APP for the complainant vehemently argued that, the accused persons having violated the provisions of FSS Act, 2006 and thereby committed offences punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the Act is very much forthcoming as per the testimonies of PW's-1 & 3. 25. The learned counsel for the accused persons emphatically argued that, the instant complaint against accused persons is not tenable as the mense rea as required U/s.48 of the Act has not been demonstrated by the complainant. It is also highlighted as to there is no any iota of evidence to incriminate the accused persons to show the accused persons had knowledge regarding the subject matter being "Unsafe for Human Consumption".
texts.respondent_arguments: The learned Sr. APP for the complainant vehemently argued that, the accused persons having violated the provisions of FSS Act, 2006 and thereby committed offences punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the Act is very much forthcoming as per the testimonies of PW's-1 & 3. 25. The learned counsel for the accused persons emphatically argued that, the instant complaint against accused persons is not tenable as the mense rea as required U/s.48 of the Act has not been demonstrated by the complainant. It is also highlighted as to there is no any iota of evidence to incriminate the accused persons to show the accused persons had knowledge regarding the subject matter being "Unsafe for Human Consumption".
